title: Cheap phones in Vietnam: prices and where to buy (2026)
description: What phones cost in Vietnam in November 2026: basic 4G phones, budget Android, iPhones and used prices, plus the VoLTE check every phone now needs.
h1: Cheap phones in Vietnam: what they cost, where to buy and what still works after 2G
intro: The cheapest phones in Vietnam are 4G basic phones and entry-level Android smartphones sold by the big national chains. 2G was switched off on 15 September 2026, so a phone without 4G calling (VoLTE) may lose calls, depending on the network and whether it falls back to 3G. Budget Android phones are good value. New iPhones are not cheap in Vietnam. Used phones from the chains' returns sections or Chợ Tốt cost less, but you need to test them before paying.
keyPoints: On 22 November 2026 the cheapest new phone we found was the Mobell M139 4G at {{vnd:250000}} (Điện Máy Chợ Lớn), and the cheapest new smartphones were the TCL 60R 5G at {{vnd:2990000}} and the Nubia V70 Design at {{vnd:3390000}} (FPT Shop), followed by the Xiaomi Redmi A7.

Vietnam switched off 2G nationwide on 15 September 2026. A phone without VoLTE (calls over 4G) may still get mobile data but may lose calls, depending on the network and whether it can fall back to 3G.
Viettel runs only 4G and 5G. VinaPhone and MobiFone still run 3G as well, and 3G is expected to close from September 2028.
New iPhones are not a bargain. Apple Vietnam charged {{vnd:28999000}} for an iPhone 17 256GB on 22 November 2026.
Thế Giới Di Động's used and returned phones come with a first-month warranty or exchange, which a private sale on Chợ Tốt does not.

sections.title: How much is a phone in Vietnam?

blocks.text: A new phone in Vietnam costs from a few hundred thousand đồng for a basic 4G handset to tens of millions for a new iPhone. Budget Android smartphones sit at the low end of that range. The table shows the price bands at the main chains, as listed on their own websites on 22 November 2026.

blocks.caption: New phone price bands in Vietnam, from retailer listings checked on 22 November 2026
rows: Điện Máy Chợ Lớn, Thế Giới Di Động
Xiaomi Redmi Note 15, Samsung Galaxy A17

blocks.text: Prices at the chains change every week with promotions, and most listings show a sale price next to a higher list price. Before you buy, compare two or three chains. On 22 November 2026 the same Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 6GB/128GB cost {{vnd:4690000}} at FPT Shop and {{vnd:4890000}} at Điện Máy Chợ Lớn.

sections.title: Cheap phones in Vietnam: the cheapest models right now

blocks.text: On 22 November 2026, according to the chains' own listings, the cheapest new phones were 4G basic phones from Mobell, Masstel and Nokia, and the cheapest smartphones were the TCL 60R 5G and the Nubia V70 Design, followed by the Xiaomi Redmi A7. For a closer look at the very bottom of the market, see [the cheapest phone in Vietnam](/guides/cheapest-phone-in-vietnam).

blocks.title: The cheapest basic phone may not have 4G
blocks.text: On 21 November 2026 the cheapest basic phone on Thế Giới Di Động's list was the Mobell M179 at {{vnd:410000}}, and its name does not mention 4G. Only 12 of the 19 basic phones on that page had 4G in the name, and none of the listings mentioned VoLTE. **Ask the shop to put your SIM in and make a test call before you pay.**

FPT Shop's listing showed an 18-month warranty badge on several of the budget models, including the TCL 60R, Redmi A7, Nubia V70 Design and POCO C81 Pro. Check the warranty on the product page, because the badges differ from model to model.
Vietnam is cheap for budget Android phones and basic phones, but not for new iPhones. A usable 5G smartphone cost about a tenth of the price of a new iPhone 17 at the chains on 22 November 2026.

According to Apple's Vietnamese online store on 22 November 2026, the iPhone 17 cost {{vnd:28999000}} for 256GB and {{vnd:35499000}} for 512GB, taxes included. On the same day CellphoneS listed the iPhone 17 256GB at {{vnd:28490000}}, and both Thế Giới Di Động and CellphoneS listed the iPhone 17 Pro 256GB at {{vnd:31990000}}, against a list price of {{vnd:34990000}}. Whether that is more than you would pay at home, and whether a tax refund applies when you leave, is covered in [is it cheaper to buy an iPhone in Vietnam](/guides/is-it-cheaper-to-buy-iphone-in-vietnam).

Chinese and Korean brands (Xiaomi, OPPO, Samsung, Honor, realme, TCL) dominate the cheaper end of the chains' listings, and that is where the savings are. For a phone you only need to work for a year or two, a mid-range Xiaomi or Samsung in the {{vnd:4690000-5990000}} band at FPT Shop (as listed on 22 November 2026) is the usual compromise.

sections.title: iPhone in Vietnam: buying used to pay less

blocks.text: A used iPhone in Vietnam costs well under the new price. According to Kenh14 (18 November 2026), a used iPhone 15 128GB sold for about {{vnd:11000000-11500000}} in early November 2026. Older models listed on Chợ Tốt cost much less again.

blocks.caption: Used phone prices in Vietnam: Kenh14 market survey (early November 2026) and Chợ Tốt listings in Ho Chi Minh City (read 21 November 2026)

blocks.text: Chợ Tốt prices are asking prices set by individual sellers, and the page itself says they are for reference only. One listing that day offered an iPhone 15 128GB at {{vnd:8300000}} in Tân Phú, well below Kenh14's range. **A price far under the going rate is a reason for extra checks, not a reason to hurry.** Listings marked “quốc tế” (international version) are phones not officially sold in Vietnam, which is the group Tuổi Trẻ News warns is most likely to have VoLTE problems.
Chợ Tốt and job ads still use the old district names. Since July 2025, official addresses in Ho Chi Minh City use new ward names instead of districts.

sections.title: Cheap used phones with a warranty

blocks.text: Thế Giới Di Động has a section for used and returned phones (“máy đổi trả”). It sells traded-in phones, display units and clearance stock with a short store warranty. On 21 November 2026 it listed a Masstel IZI 10 4G from {{vnd:150000}} and a Nokia 220 4G from {{vnd:440000}}, against new prices of {{vnd:430000}} and {{vnd:1100000}}.

items: **First month:** a fault is repaired under warranty, or you can exchange the phone or get a refund for a fee of 10% of the invoice value.
**From the second month:** the store no longer takes it back. Only the manufacturer's warranty applies, if any is left.
**Accessories:** return the charger and accessories with the phone, or pay a fee of up to 5% of the invoice value.
**Grades:** the page describes “like new” display units (battery at 85–100%), lightly worn returns and unused clearance stock. Individual listings do not always state the grade, so ask.

blocks.text: eno.vn, a free classifieds marketplace for expats and locals, has an [Electronics category](/c/electronics) where people in Vietnam post items for sale. A private sale comes with no store warranty, so test the phone the same way as on Chợ Tốt. If you are leaving Vietnam and selling your own phone, see [selling up before you leave](/selling-up-before-you-leave-vietnam).

sections.title: Will my phone work in Vietnam after the 2G switch-off?

blocks.text: Your phone is certain to work for calls in Vietnam only if it supports 4G calling (VoLTE) and VoLTE is switched on. A phone without VoLTE may lose calls after the 2G switch-off, depending on the network and whether it can fall back to 3G. According to the Radio Frequency Agency of the Ministry of Science and Technology, as reported on the Hà Tĩnh provincial portal, Vietnam switched off 2G nationwide from 15 September 2026. A 2G-only phone can no longer call, text or use mobile services.

Tuổi Trẻ News explains the trap with some 4G phones. They use 4G only for data and switch to 2G for calls, so after the switch-off they can still go online but may not be able to make or receive calls unless they can fall back to 3G. Phones most at risk are older 4G models, phones bought abroad and phones not officially sold in Vietnam.

According to Nhân Dân (16 September 2026), Viettel has already closed 3G and runs only 4G and 5G. VinaPhone and MobiFone still run 3G, 4G and 5G, and 3G is expected to close from September 2028. Activating VoLTE is free, and calls are charged as minutes on your existing plan, not taken from your data. For choosing a network and getting a number, see [the SIM and eSIM guide](/esim-vietnam-guide).

items.title: Find the VoLTE setting
items.text: On an iPhone: Settings, Mobile/Cellular, Mobile Data Options, Voice & Data, then turn on VoLTE. On Samsung: Settings, Connections, Mobile Networks. On Xiaomi or Redmi: Settings, SIM cards & mobile networks, choose the SIM, Use VoLTE. On other Android phones, look for “VoLTE” or “4G Calling”.

items.title: Check the status bar
items.text: A VoLTE or HD Voice icon shows that the phone is using 4G calling.

items.title: Make a test call
items.text: Call someone and ask them to call you back, with mobile data on and Wi-Fi off.

items.title: Go to the operator if it fails
items.text: Take the phone and SIM to a Viettel, VinaPhone or MobiFone store. Staff can check the SIM, change settings and tell you whether the phone is compatible. Whether a SIM swap is free depends on the operator.

sections.title: Where to buy a cheap phone in Vietnam

blocks.text: For a new phone, the national chains are the safest place to buy: Thế Giới Di Động, FPT Shop, CellphoneS and Điện Máy Chợ Lớn. They sell Vietnamese-market models, show warranty terms and offer 0% instalments. Used phones cost less, but the cheaper the channel, the more of the checking you have to do yourself.

blocks.text: Before you pay for any phone

items: Put your own SIM in and make a test call with Wi-Fi off.
Check that VoLTE or 4G Calling appears in the settings and can be switched on.
For a used iPhone or Android phone, check that the previous owner's account is signed out, so the phone is not locked to them.
Get an invoice from a shop. From a private seller, meet in a public place and pay only after testing.

blocks.text: If you have just arrived and are setting up a phone, a bank account and a home at the same time, [your first weeks in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/your-first-weeks-in-ho-chi-minh-city) puts them in order, and [the cost of living guide](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers) shows where a phone fits in a monthly budget.

faqs.q: How much is a phone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: A new phone in Vietnam costs least as a 4G basic handset and most as a new iPhone, which costs nearly ten times as much as the cheapest 5G Android smartphone. The price table on this page gives each band from the Thế Giới Di Động, FPT Shop, Điện Máy Chợ Lớn, CellphoneS and Apple Vietnam listings checked on 22 November 2026. Chain prices change weekly with promotions, so compare two or three chains before buying.

Phones in Vietnam are cheap at the budget end and expensive at the top. Basic 4G phones and entry-level Android smartphones from Xiaomi, TCL, Samsung and others cost little at the national chains, as the price table on this page shows. New iPhones are not a bargain: Apple Vietnam's price for an iPhone 17 is close to or above many other countries' prices, so expats rarely save by buying an iPhone in Vietnam.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to buy an iPhone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Buying a new iPhone in Vietnam is usually not cheaper than buying one abroad. On 22 November 2026 Apple's Vietnamese online store and CellphoneS listed the iPhone 17 256GB at prices shown in the iPhone section above. A used iPhone in Vietnam is far cheaper: Kenh14 reported used iPhone 15 prices in early November 2026, and older models appear on Chợ Tốt for much less.

faqs.q: Will my phone from home work in Vietnam?
faqs.a: A phone from home is certain to work for calls in Vietnam only if it supports VoLTE (4G calling) and VoLTE is turned on. Vietnam switched off 2G on 15 September 2026, so a phone without VoLTE may lose calls, depending on the network and whether it can fall back to 3G, which Viettel no longer runs. Turn on VoLTE in the mobile network settings, make a test call, and if calls fail, take the phone and SIM to a Viettel, VinaPhone or MobiFone store.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest smartphone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The cheapest new smartphone at the major Vietnamese chains on 22 November 2026 was the TCL 60R 5G 4GB/128GB at FPT Shop, on promotion. The Nubia V70 Design, Xiaomi Redmi A7, Xiaomi POCO C81 Pro and Samsung Galaxy A07 followed. The prices are in the table of cheapest models on this page. Promotional prices change often, so check the retailer's page on the day.

faqs.q: Is it safe to buy a second-hand phone in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Buying a second-hand phone in Vietnam is safe enough if you test it first and know what comes back to you. Thế Giới Di Động's used and returned phones come with a first-month warranty or exchange. Private sales on Chợ Tốt or other classifieds come with none. Test a call with your own SIM, check that VoLTE can be switched on, and make sure the previous owner's account is signed out.

faqs.q: Where can I buy a cheap phone in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: The cheapest safe places to buy a phone in Ho Chi Minh City are the national chains, Thế Giới Di Động, FPT Shop, CellphoneS and Điện Máy Chợ Lớn, which have branches across the city and sell online. Their used and returned sections cost less again. Private listings on Chợ Tốt and eno.vn's Electronics category are cheapest but have no warranty, so test before paying.
